answer: River-Marble Copper Attestation. Each agent submits a freshly cast marble whose internal copper-vein pattern is imaged, hashed, and bound to its key; the marble is then dropped into a public river channel, and later agents must locate and re-image it, signing a chain-of-custody. An attacker needs one unique physical marble per identity plus retrieval labor, making mass issuance linear in matter and search effort, not just digital cost.
